newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Korea Zinc Australia project awaits approval.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Korea Zinc Australia project awaits approval.

text.p: Korea Zinc Co Ltd's A$1 billion zinc refinery project in Queensland is still awaiting approval from the federal environment protection authority (EPA), a Queensland state government spokesman said.

"All state environment impact statements have been satisfied and we are now waiting for the federal authorities," the spokesman for Queensland economic and trade minister Doug Slack said. Documents were sent to the EPA this week, he said.

Once federal EPA requirements have been satisfied, the project would only be subject to licensing requirements with Queensland state legislation currently being drafted to secure all agreements, the spokesman said. "It is now up to Canberra when the EPA approval is given," the spokesman said.

Construction of Korea Zinc's A$530 million first stage of its Townsville refinery is expected to start early in 1997 with production from 1999. The 170,000-tonne a year project could become the world's biggest when production reaches its peak.
